requirement.title: Startup sequence
requirement.description: gmux startup: write PID file, bind Unix socket, start TmuxPoller, render Dashboard. If a stale socket/pid from a previous crash exists, clean up before proceeding.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given no previous gmux instance exists, when gmux starts, then /tmp/gmux.pid is written with the current PID, /tmp/gmux.sock is bound, poller starts, and dashboard renders.
Given /tmp/gmux.sock exists but the PID in /tmp/gmux.pid is dead, when gmux starts, then the stale socket and pid files are removed, and gmux starts normally.
Given /tmp/gmux.pid points to a live gmux process, when a second gmux attempts to start, then it exits with message "gmux already running (PID: N)" and exit code 1.

requirement.title: Shutdown sequence
requirement.description: On q, Ctrl-Q, SIGINT, or SIGTERM: stop poller, close socket, remove /tmp/gmux.sock and /tmp/gmux.pid, exit. Never touch tmux sessions.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given user presses q, when gmux shuts down, then poller stops, socket closes, /tmp/gmux.sock and /tmp/gmux.pid are removed, and the process exits with code 0.
Given gmux receives SIGTERM, when signal handler runs, then the same cleanup as q is performed.
Given 3 agent sessions are running when gmux quits, when gmux exits, then all 3 tmux sessions remain running and unaffected.

requirement.title: tmux unavailable — degraded mode
requirement.description: When tmux commands fail (not installed, server crashed), gmux enters degraded mode with stale data and a warning banner. Auto-recovers when tmux returns.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given tmux list-panes fails, when TmuxPoller retries once after 1 second and still fails, then dashboard shows banner "tmux not reachable — retrying every 5s" and session list shows last-known data with ⚠ badges.
Given gmux is in degraded mode, when tmux becomes available again, then the banner clears, session list refreshes, and normal polling resumes.
Given gmux is in degraded tmux mode, when a socket event arrives, then it is still processed normally (socket path is independent of tmux).

requirement.title: Socket unavailable — polling-only mode
requirement.description: When socket bind fails (for reasons other than a stale file from a previous instance), gmux continues with polling only and shows a warning.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given socket bind fails with a non-EADDRINUSE error, when gmux starts, then it starts successfully in polling-only mode with banner "socket unavailable — polling only".
Given gmux is in polling-only mode, when all other features are used (navigation, send-keys, create session), then they work normally.

requirement.title: send-keys failure handling
requirement.description: When tmux send-keys fails because the target pane no longer exists, remove the pane from SessionStore and notify the user.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given user sends a message to arcforge:1.1 but the pane has been closed, when send-keys returns an error, then arcforge:1.1 is removed from the session list and a "session ended" notification appears.
Given send-keys fails, when the error is handled, then no retry is attempted.

requirement.title: Configuration file
requirement.description: gmux reads configuration from ~/.config/gmux/config.json. If the file does not exist, sensible defaults are used.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given ~/.config/gmux/config.json does not exist, when gmux starts, then it uses defaults: pollInterval=3000, notificationCooldown=300000, sound=false.
Given config.json contains {"sound": true, "pollInterval": 5000}, when gmux starts, then sound is enabled and poll interval is 5 seconds. notificationCooldown uses default (300000).
Given config.json contains invalid JSON, when gmux starts, then a warning is logged and defaults are used. gmux does not crash.

requirement.title: Technology stack constraints
requirement.description: gmux is built with TypeScript, React + Ink for TUI rendering, and Vitest for testing. These choices are fixed for Phase 1 to align with the team's expertise and the proven dmux reference implementation.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the project is set up, when package.json is inspected, then it lists react, ink, and typescript as dependencies, and vitest as a dev dependency.
Given source code is written, when files are inspected, then all source files are TypeScript (.ts/.tsx) and UI components use Ink/React APIs.
